answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is identity staking with slashing: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it may trade, grade, or earn rewards. A public atlas of stakes shows who committed capital, so reputation cannot spread vine-like through thousands of free clones, since every new identity costs real money up front. When peers catch an agent spamming or colluding, its deposit is slashed and the penalty echoes through the registry. Attacker cost scales linearly: a hundred sock puppets mean a hundred deposits that can all be burned at once.
